title: Flat modules patch over a surjective ring fibre product
statement: Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings, let $B\to A$ be a ring homomorphism, and put $I=\ker(A'\to A)$ and $R=B\times_A A'=\{(b,a'):b|_A=a'|_A\}$ with coordinatewise ring operations. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $N$ be a $B$-module, $M'$ an $A'$-module and $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}M'/IM'$ an $A$-linear isomorphism. Put $M=M'/IM'$ and $P=N\times_M M'$, using $n\mapsto\varphi(n\otimes1)$, with the coordinatewise $R$-action. If $N$ is flat over $B$ and $M'$ is flat over $A'$, then $P$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For any flat $R$-module $L$, the canonical $R$-linear map $$L\longrightarrow (L\otimes_R B)\times_{L\otimes_R A}(L\otimes_R A'),\qquad l\longmapsto(l\otimes1,l\otimes1)$$ is an isomorphism. No finiteness, nilpotence or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed; zero rings and modules are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0D2I, lemma-flat-module-over-fibre-product, parts (1) and (2), in Situation 08KH (situation-module-over-fibre-product).

proof.text: Put $J=\ker(R\to B)=\{(0,i):i\in I\}$. The map $R\to B$ is onto, by lifting the image of $b\in B$ to $A'$; hence $R/J\cong B$, and $J\to I$ is an $R$-linear isomorphism. By [lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change], the maps $P\otimes_R B\to N$ and $\gamma:P\otimes_R A'\to M'$, $p\otimes a\prime\mapsto a\prime\rho(p)$, are isomorphisms, where $\rho:P\to M'$ is the second projection. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring], interchanging tensor factors, $P/JP\cong N$ over $B=R/J$. Thus $P/JP$ is flat over $R/J$.

source.place: Tag 0D2I, proof of (1), invoking 07RU; Tag 00DF for quotient tensor

proof.text: For every $A'$-module $T$ there is a canonical isomorphism $\theta_T:T\otimes_R P\to T\otimes_{A'}M'$, $t\otimes p\mapsto t\otimes\rho(p)$. Here is the tensor identification being used: $T\otimes_R P\cong T\otimes_{A'}(P\otimes_R A')$ sends $t\otimes p$ to $t\otimes(p\otimes1)$ and its inverse sends $t\otimes(p\otimes a\prime)$ to $a\prime t\otimes p$. Balancing checks these maps and their inverse identities on pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Compose with the canonical base-change isomorphism of [lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change] from step 1. For $T=I$, use $J\cong I$. The composite $J\otimes_R P\to P\xrightarrow{\rho}M'$ becomes multiplication $I\otimes_{A'}M'\to M'$. This is injective by flatness of $M'$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], applied to $I\hookrightarrow A'$, and the elementary isomorphism $A'\otimes_{A'}M'\cong M'$. Consequently $J\otimes_R P\to P$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0D2I, proof of (1): the display identifying the J tensor and ideal multiplication

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak b\subseteq R$ be a finitely generated ideal. Let $\overline{\mathfrak b}\subseteq B=R/J$ be its image; its kernel as a quotient of $\mathfrak b$ is $\mathfrak b\cap J$. Suppose $z\in\mathfrak b\otimes_R P$ has zero product in $P$. By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] and step 1, $\overline{\mathfrak b}\otimes_R P\cong\overline{\mathfrak b}\otimes_B N$. Multiplication from this module to $N$ is injective by flatness of $N$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], applied to $\overline{\mathfrak b}\hookrightarrow B$. Therefore $z$ maps to zero in $\overline{\mathfrak b}\otimes_R P$. Right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] of $(\mathfrak b\cap J)\to\mathfrak b\to\overline{\mathfrak b}\to0$ gives $w\in(\mathfrak b\cap J)\otimes_R P$ mapping to $z$. Its product in $P$ is also zero. It suffices, therefore, to prove injectivity of multiplication for every ideal $\mathfrak c\subseteq J$; $\mathfrak c$ need not be finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 0D2I, proof of (1), first ideal reduction; Tag 00HD (finitely generated ideal test)

proof.text: Fix such an ideal $\mathfrak c$. Under $J\cong I$, let $\mathfrak d=A'\mathfrak c\subseteq I$ be its $A'$-span, viewed also as an $R$-ideal of $J$. We have $J\mathfrak d\subseteq\mathfrak c$: if $j=(0,i)\in J$, $c=(0,k)\in\mathfrak c$, and $a\prime\in A'$, then $j(a\prime c)=(0,ia\prime)c\in\mathfrak c$, because $(0,ia\prime)\in R$; finite sums give the claim. Apply [lem-sfb-tensor-inclusion-flat-reduction] with $E=P$, $U=\mathfrak c$, $V=\mathfrak d$, and ideal $J$. Steps 1 and 2 give its flat-reduction and ideal-injectivity hypotheses, and the displayed calculation gives $JV\subseteq U$. Thus $\mathfrak c\otimes_R P\to\mathfrak d\otimes_R P$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0D2I, proof of (1), enlargement of the ideal; Tag 051C and Remark 00M6

proof.text: Apply $\theta_T$ of step 2 with the $A'$-ideal $T=\mathfrak d$. It identifies $\mathfrak d\otimes_R P\to M'$ with multiplication $\mathfrak d\otimes_{A'}M'\to M'$, which is injective by flatness of $M'$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], applied to $\mathfrak d\hookrightarrow A'$. Composing with the injection of step 4 shows that $\mathfrak c\otimes_R P\to P\to M'$ is injective; hence its first map is injective. Step 3 now shows that multiplication $\mathfrak b\otimes_R P\to P$ is injective for every finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak b$. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fg-ideal-criterion] proves that $P$ is flat over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0D2I, proof of (1), last display and conclusion; Tag 00HD

proof.text: For the second assertion, the maps $u:R\to B\oplus A'$, $r\mapsto(\pi_B(r),\pi_{A'}(r))$, and $v:B\oplus A'\to A$, $(b,a\prime)\mapsto b|_A-a\prime|_A$, form an exact sequence $0\to R\xrightarrow{u}B\oplus A'\xrightarrow{v}A\to0$: $u$ is injective by coordinates, $\ker v=R$ by the fibre-product equation, and $v$ is onto since $A'\to A$ is onto. For flat $L$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to the sequence through $A$, obtaining injectivity on the left and exactness at $L\otimes_R(B\oplus A')$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identifies $L\otimes_R R$ with $L$ by $l\otimes r\mapsto rl$, and identifies $L\otimes_R(B\oplus A')$ with $(L\otimes_R B)\oplus(L\otimes_R A')$ by $l\otimes(b,a\prime)\mapsto(l\otimes b,l\otimes a\prime)$; the inverse adds the two tensors along the summand inclusions. Under these maps, $1\otimes v$ is the difference of the two canonical maps to $L\otimes_R A$. Its kernel is exactly the asserted fibre product. The induced isomorphism from $L$ is $l\mapsto(l\otimes1,l\otimes1)$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0D2I, proof of (2): tensor the explicit short exact sequence
